answer: The recurrence on the Pipozop page gives C(mf) <= (s/W) C(f) + O(1), where C(f) is the time per unit of volume at parameter f. Unrolling it over the recursion depth j gives C(f) = O(sum over j from 0 to log_m f of (s/W)^j). If the ratio s/W is at most m^tau for a fixed tau below 1, every term is at most m^(tau j), so the sum is O(f^tau): the per-unit cost is a power of the parameter strictly below the first power. Two things must hold. First, the total rank s of the edge changes must be strictly less than W*m (so s/W < m); the page takes this strictness from the rank counts on the Pukezad page, which are strict because L/N < 1/2. Second, the gap must be a fixed power: s/W < m^tau with tau < 1 fixed, not merely some strict gap. The size of the saving is set by the chosen exponent tau = sigma = 1 - 2^(-50) on the Fenilov page, so the per-unit cost is O(f^(1-2^(-50))), a saving of a factor f^(2^(-50)) relative to linear in f (this last step is my own arithmetic from tau). The actual relative gap is eta = 339/22587335000000 (about 1.5e-11) for the bit network and 73/19906842167500 (about 3.7e-12) for the complex network; both exceed 20*2^(-50), about 1.8e-14, which is what makes s/W < m^tau hold. I did not open the cost-accounting page, so I did not verify how this exponent yields kappa = 2^(-182).

citations.quote: So the call makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on volume $V/W$, where $s$ is the total rank of the edge changes.
if the circuit data satisfy the shear contract with $s<Wm$ and $s/W<m^\tau$

key_idea.statement: A call at parameter mf makes s calls at parameter f, each on 1/W of the data, so the cost per unit of data at mf is at most s/W times the cost at f; when s/W is at most m^tau for a fixed tau below 1, the recursion costs a power f^tau per unit of data.

stuck.quote: A call at parameter $mf$, with $m=10^6$ the label-space dimension, splits each chunk into $m$ slots of parameter $f$.
stuck.note: I could not see why the label-space dimension is the number of slots per chunk, or what a slot is. The page gives no reason for the split factor being m.

stuck.quote: an edge's frame change costs one call at parameter $f$ on its stream per unit of rank
stuck.note: I could not see why a frame change costs one smaller call per unit of rank. I accepted it and went on to the frames page and the rank-count page to check it.

stuck.quote: The intermediate frames are therefore free, and can be chosen so that each edge change is cheap
stuck.note: The page asserts that the frames can be chosen so that edges are cheap, but does not show how that gives the rank count s. I could only connect the frame choice to the count on the Pukezad page.

stuck.quote: A wire enters and leaves each gate with that gate's label, so its signed changes telescope to sink minus source dimension
stuck.note: I followed the telescoping and the step to absolute changes Wm-2N+2L, but I could not see why the loss L is the only correction once signs are taken.

stuck.quote: For $U\subset V$, $\Pi_V-\Pi_U$ (identity on $V\cap U^\perp$, zero on $U\perp V^\perp$) has rank $\dim V-\dim U$, as does its negative.
stuck.note: I could not verify this rank claim from the page itself. I accepted it as stated.

stuck.quote: Only $X_a$'s first edge differs: at stage $1$ its first gate has label $U_a$, so $2\Pi_{U_a}$ has rank one where the dimension change is zero.
stuck.note: This is the source of the extra +N in s_b = (W_b m - 2N + 2L_b) + N. I accepted it without working through the stage-1 gate labels.

stuck.quote: [Letenat](mot) give the complex network $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$.
stuck.note: The complex strict inequality is cited to a page I did not open, so I accepted it on the citation.

stuck.quote: Here $j$ means the recursion depth, the number of levels below the top call, not the stage number as on [Pukezad](dol)
stuck.note: j is redefined here with a meaning different from the Pukezad page, so I had to decode which j is meant in the unrolled sum.

stuck.quote: otherwise its last term, below $m^{\tau\log_m f}=f^\tau$, dominates
stuck.note: The page says the last term dominates when s/W is above 1. I followed it, but I did not see why the geometric terms add up to a constant times the last one; I accepted it.

The page sets tau = sigma = 1 - 2^(-50) and calls these values conservative without saying what they are conservative against. I could not tell whether tau is derived from the rank count or chosen as a parameter.

stuck.quote: $W$ (stream count): The fixed number of streams into which rows are dealt. From [Legafod](zaz).
stuck.note: W was undefined until I opened the stream-operations page, where it is the fixed number of streams that rows are dealt into cyclically.

reason: I answered, but my confidence is moderate. The recurrence C(mf) <= (s/W) C(f) + O(1) and its unrolling, the strict inequality s < Wm, the exponent tau = 1 - 2^(-50), and the margins (eta about 1.5e-11 bit and 3.7e-12 complex, both above 20*2^(-50)) are all stated on the pages I opened, and I checked the two eta values by hand. Several steps, including why a frame change counts as one call per unit of rank and why the extra +N appears, were accepted from the text without full derivation. I opened 7 of the 15 allowed pages and did not open the cost-accounting page or the Letenat page.
